Standard: Blades and disks do not contact any static parts of the engine other than seals, shrouds, or any other intentional contact surfaces when operating at all points within the engine operating envelope, including surge and stall occurrences, and bowed rotor starts. Materials intended as rub couples are fully characterized across the range of operational conditions and incursion rates. Seals and clearances remain effective under all internal and external loads, manufacturing tolerances, cold and hot day operation including transient thermal conditions. Blade failure and blade or disk rubbing does not result in uncontained fire. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Examination of material rub couples verifies capability compatible with engine operation and incursion rates. Analysis.
  (1) Analysis verifies that positive clearances, both axial and radial, and effective sealing exist under all operational conditions and maneuver load conditions.
  (2) Rotor dynamics and thermal containment analyses verify capability under blade out and rub conditions. Test.
    (1) Lab test: Engine tests in a ground-based sea level and altitude test cell verify clearance predictions under steady state and transient operation. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
    (2) Flight test: Flight tests verify maneuver effects. Instrumentation and dimensional inspections before and after testing are used to confirm analytical predictions.
